@attributes.Name: DACBE Disable Hblank Extension For Vblank Auto Gating

Description.#text: By default, if SDP Splitting is enabled in AUD_DP_2DOT0_CTRL bit-field "Enable SDP Split", usage of the hblank extension fix for all lines in vblank is disabled automatically. Setting this bit removes the automatic behavior, and usage of the hblank extension fix for all vblank lines will depend only on the bit-field "DACBE Disable Hblank Extension for Full Vblank".

@attributes.Name: DACBE Disable Hblank Extension for Vblank

Description.#text: Setting this bit disables application of the hblank extension logic to all lines within vblank. Instead hblank extension will be applied only to lines 2 to 6 in vblank, or will be disabled if bit-field "DACBE Disable AIF and ATS hblank extension fix" is set.

@attributes.Name: DACBE Enable Hblank Extension Auto Gating

Description.#text: By default, usage of hblank extension for lines 2 through 6 in vblank remains enabled regardless of the SDP splitting setting. Setting this bit enables automatic gating of the hblank extension feature if SDP Splitting is enabled in AUD_DP_2DOT0_CTRL bit-field "Enable SDP Split".

@attributes.Name: DACBE Disable DP1 Timestamp Available Fix

Description.#text: Setting this bit disables revisions to the timestamp available signal which avoids data changes while the ATS packet is being processed. By default the revised signal is used.

@attributes.Name: DACBE Disable DP1 Lane Buffer FIFO Get Fix

Description.#text: Setting this bit disables revisions to the get signal for the DP1 lane buffer FIFO. By default the revised signal is used.
When set disables suppression of the hblank when hblank rises before hblank early.

@attributes.Name: DACBE Disable AIF and ATS hblank extension fix

Description.#text: When set disables extension of the hblank during vblank lines 2-6 to allow room for completion of AIF and ATS packets.

Setting this bit forces complete disabling of the DP mode change trigger to re-send AIF and ATS packets, which can occur anywhere in the frame, and ensures they will only be sent as normal in vblank lines 2-6. By default DP mode change disabling is based on the status of the "DACBE Disable DP Mode Change Auto Gating" and "DACBE Disable AIF and ATS hblank extension fix" bit-fields.

@attributes.Name: DACBE Disable DP Mode Change Auto Gating

Description.#text: By default, the DP mode change will automatically be disabled if the AIF/ATS hblank extension fix remains enabled. Setting this bit removes the automatic dependency on the "DACBE Disable AIF and ATS hblank extension fix" bit-field, and allows the DP mode-change to be controlled exclusively by the "DACBE Disable DP Mode Change" bit-field.

@attributes.Name: DACBE Disable DP mode change buffering

Description.#text: When set disables buffering the DP mode change pulse when the mixer FSM is not in the idle state.

@attributes.Name: DACBE Disable audio on first hblank in vblank

Description.#text: When set disables allowing transmission of AMS packets during the first hblank in vblank by reverting to legacy FSM behavior.

@attributes.Name: DACBE DP2 Disable wait to idle arc on hblank_end

Description.#text: When set disables moving from wait to idle on hblank_end for the lanebuf write FSM for DP2.

Description.#text: By default, dacbeunit will maintain its stall counter in sync with hdmiunit using a packet end indicator. Setting this bit disables the usage of this synchronization method.

@attributes.Name: DACRG Disable HDMI Vblank Masking for PD Bit Changes

Description.#text: By default, in HDMI mode changes to the Presence Detect bit which occur during the HDMI vblank period will be buffered until the falling edge of vblank. Setting this bit disables this behavior and reverts to allowing the PD bit changes to take effect immediately regardless of HDMI vblank.

Description.#text: Setting this bit enables resetting the dacbeunit un-stall counter after audio packets are completed, to ensure synchronization. By default this fix is disabled, and sync is maintained by the HDMI FRL Clock Gating Based enable.

This register provides per-pipe DisplayPort related controls for DP1, DP2, and shared functionality. For DP2, this bit can be set to enable multi-stream codec features, including device select based pipe to pin node mapping and related MST mode verb responses. This bit should be set when this pipe is attached to a port configured for DP2 with multiple streams.

When set to this value, maximum of two samples(each sample has 2 channels data for layout0 and 8 channels data in layout 1 mode) in the buffer are unloaded on the line in the hblank region.

Description.#text: This register allows programming of parameters related to HDMI2.1 for the back-end processing unit within audio. These settings must be programmed during mode set enabling and should not be changed once video and audio is enabled.

When enabled, the number of audio packets ready to be sent will be dynamically calculated for each hblank. When disabled, a default amount of space will be reserved on every hblank for audio packets according to the value specified in bit-field "Default Audio Packet Count".

Specifies the amount of space reserved every hblank to send audio packets, regardless of how many are available each hblank. When bit-field "Enable Time Borrowing Optimization" is set, this value will be ignored. The default value of 18 packets (12h) is also the maximum allowed value that should be programmed.

Specifies the minimum number of tcclks at which hblank early will rise before hblank. The hblank early indication will be used to capture the number of audio packets to be sent when bit-field "Enable Time Borrowing Optimization" is set. The default is 32 tcclks.

Enables measurements and reporting of FSM states and flags.
Measurement and reporting of FSM states and flags disabled, all stored values reset.
Measurement and reporting of FSM states and flags enabled.

This bit field determines how the Measurement Result will be updated. When Measurement Type is set to 0000b (Flags) or 0001b (FSM States) the result value will reported continuously regardless of this bit field's setting. By default the un-modified hblank is used when SDP Splitting is enabled.
Measurements not performed, resets all stored values.
Measurement completed once and held, reported directly in Measurement Result.
Measurements completed continuously, reported directly in Measurement Result.
Measurements completed continuously, lowest value observed so far reported in Measurement Result.
Measurements completed continuously, highest value observed so far reported in Measurement Result.
Use only SDP Splitting generated hblanks, measurements completed continuously (Running mode).
Use the full SDP Splitting generated hblank, measurements completed continuously (Running mode).
Results value will provide a free-running counter of TCCLK (increments every 256 clocks) which can be set by toggling bit 31 (disable/enable).
This bit field selects which parameter will be measured. When set to 0000b (Flags) or 0001b (FSM States) the result value will reported continuously regardless of the Measurement Mode setting.

p.#text: Reports the current states of flags regardless of Measurement Mode setting, as detailed below:
Measurement Result [23:18]: Reserved.
Measurement Result [17:17]: Flag: DP Mode-change occurred modified version.
Measurement Result [16:16]: Flag: DP Mode-change occurred original version.
Measurement Result [15:15]: Flag: Hblank Inversion fix active with hblank inversion present.
Measurement Result [14:14]: Flag: Hblank Inversion fix active.
Measurement Result [13:13]: Flag: Hblank Extension fix active during hactive.
Measurement Result [12:12]: Flag: Hblank Extension fix active.
Measurement Result [11:11]: Flag: SDP Split GEN occurred in hactive of vactive.
Measurement Result [10:10]: Flag: SDP Split GEN wrap pause enforced or GEN restricted.
Measurement Result [09:09]: Flag: SDP Split GEN wrap occurred.
Measurement Result [08:08]: Flag: SDP Split GEN occurred.
Measurement Result [07:07]: Flag: SDP Split HOLD occurred.
Measurement Result [06:06]: Flag: DP2 Lane buffer full indicator set.
Measurement Result [05:05]: Flag: DP2 Lane buffer read FSM not idle after hblank end.
Measurement Result [04:04]: Flag: ATS or AIF sent outside of horizontal lines 2-7 within vblank.
Measurement Result [03:03]: Flag: Hblank rise at or before hblank_early rise (inversion).
Measurement Result [02:02]: Flag: Audio done pulse during hactive.
Measurement Result [01:01]: Flag: Mixer FSM not idle after hblank end.
Measurement Result [00:00]: Flag: Mixer FSM not idle.
Reports the current states of dacbeunit state machines regardless of Measurement Mode setting, as detailed below:
Measurement Result [23:20]: Dacbe DP2 Assembler Lanebuf Read FSM state.
Measurement Result [19:16]: Dacbe DP2 Assembler Lanebuf Write FSM state.
Measurement Result [15:12]: Dacbe DP2 Assembler Xclk Fifo Read FSM state.
Measurement Result [11:08]: Dacbe DP2 SDP Splitting FSM state.
Measurement Result [07:00]: Dacbe DP Mixer FSM state.

Description.#text: Counts the number of tcclks between the rising edge of hblank_early and the rising edge of hblank.
Counts the number of tcclks between the rising edge and falling edge of hblank.
Counts the number of tcclks between the rising edge and falling edge of hblank, when the dpt stall signal is low.

Counts the total tcclks (lower 12 bits) and the tcclks when the dpt stall is low (upper 12 bits) between hblank rising edge and the dacbe_dpt_SE pulse, to determine the ratio of available tcclks for audio versus the total tcclks during audio transmission.
Counts the total tcclks (lower 12 bits) during hblank and the total tcclks between hblank rising edge and the dacbe_dpt_SE pulse (upper 12 bits), to determine the percentage of hblank used for audio.
Counts the number of tcclks between the falling edge of two successive hblanks (measures line time).
Counts the number of horizontal lines between the rising and falling edge of vblank.
Counts the number of horizontal lines between two successive rising edges of vblank.
For DP2 this bit field reports the total number of samples which have entered the pipeline between successive audio_pkt_done pulses, for DP1 the result will be zero.

Counts the number of times SDPs are split using the HOLD state (lower 12 bits) and using the GEN state where wrapping occurs in vactive (upper 12 bits), during the current video frame.
Counts the number of horizontal lines taken to complete SDP splitting using the HOLD state (lower 12 bits) and using the GEN state where wrapping occurs in vactive (upper 12 bits).
Counts the number of generated hblanks during Vactive (lower 12 bits) and Vblank (upper 12 bits) during the current video frame.
Reports the results of each measurement according to the Measurement Mode and Measurement Type settings.
This register provides backup controls for the DP SDP Generator audio pipeline.

Setting this bit forces All DP SG pipeline logic into reset. Clearing this bit releases the reset state to resume normal operation. SW must perform the setting and clearing of this bit by successive writes (not automatic).

Setting this bit forces the shared Channel Mapper logic into reset. Clearing this bit releases the reset state to resume normal operation. SW must perform the setting and clearing of this bit by successive writes (not automatic).

Setting this bit forces the storage RAM into reset. Clearing this bit releases the reset state to resume normal operation. SW must perform the setting and clearing of this bit by successive writes (not automatic).

Setting this bit forces the Stream XCLK FIFO into reset. Clearing this bit releases the reset state to resume normal operation. SW must perform the setting and clearing of this bit by successive writes (not automatic).

Setting this bit forces the Info-Frame FSM in CDCLK and related logic into reset. Clearing this bit releases the reset state to resume normal operation. SW must perform the setting and clearing of this bit by successive writes (not automatic).

Setting this bit forces the Info-Frame XCLK FIFO into reset. Clearing this bit releases the reset state to resume normal operation. SW must perform the setting and clearing of this bit by successive writes (not automatic).

Setting this bit forces All DP SG Stream logic into reset. Clearing this bit releases the reset state to resume normal operation. SW must perform the setting and clearing of this bit by successive writes (not automatic).

Setting this bit forces All DP SG Timestamp logic into reset. Clearing this bit releases the reset state to resume normal operation. SW must perform the setting and clearing of this bit by successive writes (not automatic).

Setting this bit forces All DP SG InfoFrame logic into reset. Clearing this bit releases the reset state to resume normal operation. SW must perform the setting and clearing of this bit by successive writes (not automatic).

Setting this bit forces All DP SG Control logic into reset. Clearing this bit releases the reset state to resume normal operation. SW must perform the setting and clearing of this bit by successive writes (not automatic).

Setting this bit forces the shared channel mapper to be used regardless of other settings. By default the unified channel mapper is only used when DP is enabled and legacy DP mode is disabled (SDP Generator logic is in use).
Shared channel mapper will automatically be enabled only when DP is enabled and legacy DP mode is disabled (SDP Generator logic is in use).
Shared channel mapper will be enabled for use regardless of other settings.

Setting this bit enables bypassing the native channel mapping functions of the HDMI related logic, so that the unified mapper logic can be used for channel mapping instead. This setting should only be used in conjunction with setting bit-field "Force Mapper Enable".
HDMI logic native channel mapping functions will be used.
HDMI logic native channel mapping functions will be bypassed, shared channel mapper will be used instead.

Setting this bit enables bypassing the native channel mapping functions of the legacy DP related logic for 8b/10b and 128b/132b, so that the unified mapper logic can be used for channel mapping instead. This setting should only be used in conjunction with setting bit-field "Force Mapper Enable".
Legacy DP logic native channel mapping functions will be used for 8b/10b and 128b/132b mode.
Legacy DP logic native channel mapping functions will be bypassed, shared channel mapper will be used instead for 8b/10b and 128b/132b mode.

Reserved for future use.
Reserved for future use.
Reserved for future use.

@attributes.Name: Disable AMS Sending Debug Data Upon Errors

Description.#text: By default, under specific illegal conditions the AMS logic will transmit a 0xDEADBEEF pattern for easier identification during debug. Setting this bit disables this behavior and reverts to transmitting 0x0 in the same illegal conditions.
Enable sending debug pattern upon illegal conditions.
Disable sending debug pattern upon illegal conditions.

@attributes.Name: Disable AIF FSM Restriction On Shutdown

Description.#text: By default when a shutdown occurs, the DIP transfer FSM will be reset and gated from leaving the IDLE state again while audio remains disabled to ensure a clean state on resume. Setting this bit disables this FSM gating and restores its transitions to legacy behavior even for DP SG mode. The next DIP may be transferred to storage during or after shutdown.
Enable gating the DIP transfer FSM from any additional activity once audio has been disabled.
Disable gating the DIP transfer FSM from additional activity, restoring legacy behavior.

@attributes.Name: Disable AIF Early Exit On Shutdown

Description.#text: By default when a shutdown occurs, DACBE will exit from transferring AIF data to DPT as soon as the current InfoFrame is completed (before all enabled AIFs have been transmitted). Setting this bit disables this earlier exist behavior, and will postpone disable completion and clock gating during shutdown until all enabled infoframes have been transferred to DPT.
Enable early exit from AIF transfer during shutdown, exit at nearest safe opportunity.
Disable early exit from AIF transfer during shutdown, wait until all enabled infoframes are transferred before entering shutdown.

@attributes.Name: Disable Sync Reset Wait for Busy

Description.#text: Setting this bit disables waiting for Audio Stream and Audio InfoFrame logic to complete ongoing data transfers with DPT before issuing a sync reset.
Graceful sync reset remains in use, logic will wait for ongoing data transfers to complete before reset occurs.
Immediate sync reset will be used, regardless of current data transfer state with DPT.

@attributes.Name: Enable Resend of AIF and ATS on Mode Change

Description.#text: Setting this bit enables triggering a re-send of the AIF and ATS SDPs at any time during the video frame when an audio mode change occurs. This resend is in addition to the normal transmission of AIF and ATS SDPs during vblank.
Resending of the AIF and ATS SDPs upon mode change is enabled.
Resending of the AIF and ATS SDPs upon mode change is disabled.

@attributes.Name: Disable Mode Change Resend Wait for InfoFrame

Description.#text: Setting this bit disables waiting for the InfoFrame logic when issuing a mode change trigger to DPT. Only valid if bit-field "Enable Resend of AIF and ATS on Mode Change" is set.
Wait for InfoFrame logic enabled.
Wait for InfoFrame logic disabled.

@attributes.Name: Disable Mode Change Resend Wait for Timestamp

Description.#text: Setting this bit disables waiting for the timestamp accumulator when issuing a mode change trigger to DPT. Only valid if bit-field "Enable Resend of AIF and ATS on Mode Change" is set.
Wait for Timestamp accumulator enabled.
Wait for Timestamp accumulator disabled.

This setting determines the number of link clocks the audio control logic waits before proceeding to enabled or disabled states. During enabling the wait ensures gated clocks have time to start running. During disabling the wait ensures the sync reset has time to reach all clock domains before disabling the gated clock.
Number of clocks to wait before proceeding to enabled or disabled state.

This register controls the periodic re-transmission of Audio Timestamp and Audio InfoFrame SDPs during long vblank periods for this pipe (each pipe has a separate instance of this register). Setting this bit enables the re-transmission of Audio Timestamp and Audio InfoFrame SDPs during Vblank at a fixed, repeated interval determined by the "Periodic Audio Duration". This re-transmission is in addition to the normal per-frame transmission of Audio Timestamp and Audio InfoFrame SDPs.
Periodic audio is disabled. Audio Timestamp and Audio InfoFrame SDPs will only be sent once during vblank (normal per-frame transmission).
Periodic audio is enabled. Audio Timestamps and Audio InfoFrame SDPs will be re-sent during Vblank based on the "Periodic Audio Duration" setting (in addition to normal per-frame transmission).

This setting determines how many additional horizontal lines in vblank will occur before each re-transmission of Audio Timestamp and Audio InfoFrame SDPs is triggered. This value must be determined by SW based on the current horizontal line time and vblank maximum size to ensure a re-transmission rate of Audio Timestamps and Audio InfoFrames equal to the standard frame time at the normal/native refresh rate of the monitor. This bit-field must be programmed to a value greater than 1.

This bit-field determines how the stream data will be packed into DSO packets, to provide options for better timestamp accuracy or lighter capture BW.

Stream Data will be sent when valid ends (after 1, 2, 3 or 4 bytes received). Unfilled slots within the DSO packet will be zero padded. Capture timestamps will be the most accurate but potentially more DSO BW may be used.
Stream Data will be sent when 4 bytes have been collected or when the link frame ends if less than 4 are collected at this time. Capture timestamps may be less accurate, but less DSO BW may be used.

This register can be used to mask (filter) Link Commands from being captured by the audio DSO logic. The value written to this register will be applied as a mask according to the settings in the AUD_DSO_PA_LINK_CONFIG register. Each mask enable setting in AUD_DSO_PA_LINK_CONFIG determines how many bits from the Link Command Mask Value are actually used, according to the field size within the DSO packet that this mask is being applied to. This register should only be updated while the AUD_DSO_PA_LINK_CONFIG bit-field "Link Command Capture Enable" is set to 0b (capture disabled).

This value will be applied as a bit-wise mask to parts of the Audio DSO Link Command packet according to the current settings in the AUD_DSO_PA_LINK_CONFIG register. Setting a bit to 1b will mask any Link Command containing a value of 1b in the same bit position within the field enabled for masking. Only the bits from 0 up to the size of the field(s) selected for masking will be used, upper bits from this register will be ignored.

This register can be used to mask (filter) Link Events from being captured by the audio DSO logic. The value written to this register will be applied as a mask according to the settings in the AUD_DSO_PA_LINK_CONFIG register. Each mask enable setting in AUD_DSO_PA_LINK_CONFIG determines how many bits from the Link Event Mask Value are actually used, according to the field size within the DSO packet that this mask is being applied to. This register should only be updated while the AUD_DSO_PA_LINK_CONFIG bit-field "Link Event Capture Enable" is set to 0b (capture disabled).

This value will be applied as a bit-wise mask to parts of the Audio DSO Link Event packet according to the current settings in the AUD_DSO_PA_LINK_CONFIG register. Setting a bit to 1b will mask any Link Event containing a value of 1b in the same bit position within the field enabled for masking. Only the bits from 0 up to the size of the field(s) selected for masking will be used, upper bits from this register will be ignored.

This register can be used to match (select) Link Commands to be captured by the audio DSO logic (all non-matching Link Commands will be filtered out). The value written to this register will be applied as a match according to the settings in the AUD_DSO_PA_LINK_CONFIG register. Each match enable setting in AUD_DSO_PA_LINK_CONFIG determines how many bits from the Link Command Match Value are actually used, according to the field size within the DSO packet that this match is being applied to. This register should only be updated while the AUD_DSO_PA_LINK_CONFIG bit-field "Link Command Capture Enable" is set to 0b (capture disabled).

This value will be applied as a bit-wise match to parts of the Audio DSO Link Command packet according to the current settings in the AUD_DSO_PA_LINK_CONFIG register. Setting a bit to 1b will keep any Link Command containing a value of 1b in the same bit position within the field enabled for masking, all others will be filtered out. Only the bits from 0 up to the size of the field(s) selected for masking will be used, upper bits from this register will be ignored.

This register provides status information for the Link Command and Link Event capture functions. Unless mentioned otherwise in the bit-fields of this register, all status bits can be cleared using the Link Command or Link Event Sync Reset bits within the AUD_DSO_PA_LINK_CONFIG register.

This read-only bit indicates that the internal FIFO used to process stream data has overflowed. At least one byte of Stream Data has not been successfully captured. Please use the AUD_DSO_LINK_EVENT_CTL bit-field "Link Event Sync Reset" to clear this error status. Consider applying mask/match settings to reduce capture BW.

This read-only bit indicates that the internal FIFO used to process stream data is full. No data has yet been lost, however this indicates the debug logic may be close to its BW limits. Please use the AUD_DSO_LINK_EVENT_CTL bit-field "Link Event Sync Reset" to clear this error status. Consider applying mask/match settings to reduce capture BW.

Description.#text: These registers contain the HDMI/DP data block from the EDID. The graphics driver reads the EDID and writes the structure to these registers. The vendor specific data block may be longer than 8 bytes, but the driver must not write more than 48 bytes to the buffer. The EDID format is Version 3 within the CEA-861B specification. The HDMI/DP Vendor Specific Data Block is described in version 1.1 of the HDMI specification. These values are returned from the device as the HDMI/DP Vendor Specific Data Block response to a Get HDMI/DP Widget command. Writing sequence:

li.#text: Video software sets ELD invalid, and sets the ELD access address to 0, or to the desired DWORD to be written.
Video software writes ELD data 1 DWORD at a time. The ELD access address autoincrements with each DWORD write, wrapping around to address 0 when the max buffer address size of 0xF has been reached.
Please note that software must write an entire DWORD at a time.
Please note that the audio driver checks the valid bit with each byte read of the ELD. This means that the video driver can unilaterally write ELD irrespective of audio driver ELD read status.
Video software sets the ELD access address to 0, or to the desired DWORD to be read.
Video software reads ELD data 1 DWORD at a time. The ELD access address autoincrements with each DWORD read, wrapping around to address 0 when the max buffer address size of 0xF has been reached.

Immediate Command Write (ICW): The command to be sent to the codec via the Immediate Command mechanism is written to this register. The command stored in this register is sent out over the link during the next available frame after a 1 is written to the ICB bit.

Immediate Result Valid (IRV): This bit is set to a 1 by hardware when a new response is latched into the IRR register. This is a status flag indicating that software may read the response from the Immediate Response register. Software must clear this bit (by writing a one to it) before issuing a new command so that the software may determine when a new response has arrived.
Response_read
Response_available

Immediate Command Busy (ICB): When this bit as read as a 0 it indicates that a new command may be issued using the Immediate Command mechanism. When this bit transitions from a 0 to a 1 (via software writing a 1), the controller issues the command currently stored in the Immediate Command register to the codec over the link. When the corresponding response is latched into the Immediate Response register, the controller hardware sets the IRV flag and clears the ICB bit back to 0. Note that an Immediate Command must not be issued while the CORB/RIRB mechanism is operating, otherwise the responses conflict. This must be enforced by software.

Command_available

Description.#text: Setting this bit uses the Clock Stop tracking FSM state as an additional qualifier to ensure the Clock Stop wake request is not made outside of Clock Stop.

@attributes.Name: Disable Legacy MST Mode Auto Set

Description.#text: When Soundwire is enabled, the MST (edp12) mode which is normally controlled through the legacy HDA 781H Vendor Verb will be automatically based on the transcoder MST mode. Setting this bit disables automatic determination of this value, which can then be controlled with the "Enable Legacy MST Mode bit-field".
When Soundwire is enabled and the bit-field "Disable Legacy MST Mode Auto Set" is set to 1b, this bit-field can be used to manually control the state of legacy MST (edp12) mode.

When Soundwire is enabled, this bit field controls the All-Pins mode which is normally controlled through the legacy HDA 781H Vendor Verb. For Soundwire All-Pins mode will be driven high by default, setting this bit will drive the signal low.
This register provides status and controls related to the Clock Stop state of the Soundwire Link.
This bit-field indicates the current state of the Soundwire link in regards to Clock Stop.
Soundwire link has not been enabled or the clock is not yet running.
Soundwire link has been enabled and clock toggling has been detected.
Soundwire link is in the process of transition into the Clock Stop state.
Soundwire link is in the Clock Stop state.

This bit-field can be used by the GFX driver to indicate that the Soundwire link may not be transitioned into the Clock Stop state. In the event of a Clock Stop Prepare request from the Controller, if this bit-field is set the Codec will not respond back with the Clock Stop Ready acknowledgement. If the Soundwire link is already in the Clock Stop state, this bit-field will have no effect, and GFX driver can request a wake from Clock Stop by setting the "Clock Stop Wake Request" bit-field.
Indicates that the Soundwire link may be transitioned into the Clock Stop state if requested by the Controller.
Indicates that the Soundwire link may not be transitioned into the Clock Stop state if requested by the Controller.

This bit can be set to initiate a request from the codec to the controller to bring the Soundwire link out of the "Clock Stop" state. Once the "Clock Stop Status" bit-field no longer indicates Clock Stop State, this bit should be cleared. By default this bit is solely controlled by the GFX driver (setting and clearing). When set outside of the Clock Stop state, this bit has no effect.
Indicates that either there is no active wake request.
Indicates a Clock Stop wake has been requested.

This register controls usage and enumeration of the Soundwire interface for audio.

By default the legacy Azalia 3-pin link protocol will be used. Setting this bit will select and enable usage of the Soundwire protocol. This bit must be set before the audio link can be used, and cannot be changed until audio is completely disabled.
Legacy HD Audio protocol will be used for audio.
Soundwire protocol will be used for audio.
Setting this bit will force the Soundwire handling logic into a reset state, clearing this bit will resume normal operation.

Setting this bit controls whether the incoming Soundwire Clock is doubled (if receiving SDW 1X CLK) or divided (if receiving the SDW 2X CLK). If this setting needs to be changed from default, SW must write this bit first before setting the Enable Soundwire bit, and this bit must not be changed while the Enable Soundwire bit is set.
The audio controller provides the SDW 1X CLK and the codec doubles it locally to generate SDW 2X CLK.
The audio controller provides the SDW 2X CLK and the codec divides it locally to generate SDW 1X CLK.

Setting this bit controls the polarity of the 1X clock generated within display, based on the 2X clock from the controller. If this setting needs to be changed from default, SW must write this bit first before setting the Enable Soundwire bit.
The Soundwire 1X clock used for enumeration will remain un-modified.
The Soundwire 1X clock used for enumeration will be inverted in polarity.

This bit-field indicates whether the AUD driver has specifically requested de-enumeration by setting all streams to the PS4 state. It will be set when AUD driver writes the Soundwire SDCA register SDCA_PDE_REQUESTED_PS to PS4 for all streams, and will be cleared when any stream has left the PS4 state due to re-enumeration or register writes from the AUD driver or GFX driver. Note that this bit-field does not indicate overall enumeration status, which can be tracked using the "Link Enable Status" bit-field.
Codec has not de-enumerated due to an AUD driver request for PS4 state on all streams.
Codec has de-enumerated due to an AUD driver request for PS4 state on all streams.

Indicates the current status of the codec on the Soundwire link. This bit will be set after the "Link Enable Request" bit-field has been set, the Soundwire link is running, and the codec as successfully enumerated on the link. This bit will be cleared when the link enters the Clock Stop state, which is also indicated in the "Clock Stop Status" bit-field.
Codec is not currently enumerated on the Soundwire link.
Codec is enumerated on the Soundwire link.
Setting this bit prevents automatic de-enumeration based on the AUD driver setting all streams to the PS4 state.

Setting this bit triggers the start of the enumeration process. The codec will attempt to join the Soundwire link. The "Link Enable Status" bit-field indicates the current status of the link based on this request.
Codec is not joined to the link, and is not attempting to join the link.
Codec is attempting to join the link, or has already joined the link.
This register allows read-only access to loopback stream debug and Soundwire Classic register space signals.

p.#text: This register provides control of specific bit-fields within the Soundwire Device ID structure which GFX driver will populate based on the PCI Graphics Device ID before initiating enumeration. These values are read by Audio SW through the Soundwire Classic SCP_DevID_0 through SCP_DevID_5 registers. These values will also need to be restored by the GFX driver on resuming from PG0 off, before re-initiating codec enumeration.

Description.#text: Controls the Unique ID value within the Soundwire Classic SCP_DevID_0 register bits [3:0]. This 4-bit value may be used for unique identification of this device when multiple identical parts are present in a system.

Controls the Part ID value within the Soundwire Classic SCP_DevID_3 (upper 8 bits) and SCP_DevID_4 (lower 8 bits) registers. This 16-bit value is used to identify the display IP version contained in this device.

p.#text: This register provides backup control of specific bit-fields within the Soundwire Device ID structure which are not expected to change but are defaulted to the correct specification defined values and provided for SW control should adjustments become necessary in the future. If SW adjustments are necessary, these values should be adjusted by the GFX driver during normal setup or when restoring from PG0 off, before initiating codec enumeration.

Description.#text: Controls the Version value within the Soundwire Classic SCP_DevID_0 register bits [7:4]. The default value of 0011b indicates Soundwire Version 1.2

Controls the Manufacturer ID value within the Soundwire Classic SCP_DevID_1 (upper 8 bits) and SCP_DevID_2 (lower 8 bits) registers. The default value of 0105h indicates the manufacturer of this device is Intel.

Controls the Class value within the Soundwire Classic SCP_DevID_5 register bits [7:0]. The default value of 1h indicates this device implements SDCA specification registers, which provide additional class information.

This register provides configuration and control for each of the four audio DIP types. The GFX driver will use this register to configure all the required DIPs for the outgoing audio stream transmitted on this pipe before enabling the audio stream for playback.

This bit-field selects which of the four DIP types will be controlled by all of the remaining bit-fields in this register. Once this value is updated, reads and writes for the remaining bit-fields in this register will be addressed to the selected DIP type.
Selects the Audio Info Frame DIP type.
Selects the Audio Copy Protection DIP type.
Selects the International Recording Standard Code 1 DIP type.

This bit field selects the transmit frequency for the DIP type selected in the "DIP Type" bit-field. By default all DIPs are disabled.
Transmission of this DIP type is disabled.
This DIP type will be transmitted only once at the next available opportunity during the video frame.
This DIP type will be transmitted for each available opportunity during the video frame.
This bit-field indicates the total DIP byte storage size including the header and payload bytes.
Indicates storage for a total of 30 bytes.

This bit field allows selection of which byte index within the total DIP byte storage will be read or written when the DIP Data Value bit-field is accessed. By default this index value is auto-incremented for each successive read or write access of the DIP Data Value bit-field.

This bit field allows reading and writing of the DIP byte stored at the currently selected byte index for the currently selected DIP Type. Successive reads and writes to this register will automatically increment the byte index, which can also be manually controlled with the DIP Data Index bit-field. During auto-increment the byte index will roll over to 0 when it has reached the highest value.

The values will persist while PG0 remains on, and should not be changed by the GFX driver after codec enumeration has occurred.

These bytes should be set by the GFX driver during initial setup or after resuming from PG0 off states, before initiating codec enumeration through the AUD_SDW_CTL register. The values will persist while PG0 remains on, and should not be changed by the GFX driver after codec enumeration has occurred.

The values will persist while PG0 remains on, and should not be changed by the GFX driver after codec enumeration has occurred.

This register provides Soundwire Keep Alive related controls for this pipe instance and the associated Soundwire outgoing audio stream.
Indicates the current state of the audio stream in relation to Keep Alive behaviors.
Stopped - Audio stream is not configured for any channels.
Waiting - Audio stream is configured for > 0 channels but no real data has yet been received.
Running - Audio stream is configured and real sample data has been received.
Indicates whether Keep Alive data is actively being sent or not.
Keep Alive is idle or disabled, not keep alive data is being sent.
Keep Alive data is actively being sent.
Indicates which type of Keep Alive data has been selected through the Soundwire SDCA register SDCA_OT_KEEP_ALIVE.
Silent data will be sent when Keep Alive is active.
Tone Generator data will be sent when Keep Alive is active.
Indicates whether Keep Alive has been enabled through the Soundwire SDCA register SDCA_OT_KEEP_ALIVE and not force-disabled by any chickenbits.
Keep Alive is disabled.
Keep Alive is enabled.
Setting this bit forces the output of keep alive data regardless of the presence of real stream data.
Keep Alive Force Mode is disabled, keep alive data will only be sent when Keep Alive is active (when real stream data has not been received).
Keep Alive Force Mode is enabled, keep alive data will be sent regardless of Keep Alive status or the presence of real stream data.

@attributes.Name: Disable Keep Alive Sample Flat Indicator

Description.#text: By default, when Keep Alive is active for HDMI, the sample flat bit within the audio sample packet header for each sub-packet that is present will be set. Setting this bit disables the indicator to dacfpunit to set the Sample Flat bit.
When Keep Alive is active, a sample flat indicator will be sent to dacfpunit for usage in HDMI packetization.
When Keep Alive is active, a sample flat indicator will not be sent to dacfpunit for usage in HDMI packetization.

@attributes.Name: Disable Keep Alive Flush Real Samples

Description.#text: By default, when Keep Alive is active, any incoming real samples from the Soundwire link into the XCLK FIFO are flushed by pulling them from the XCLK FIFO but not using them. This ensures stale data does not accumulate in the XCLK FIFO which may unintentionally be sent later when keep alive is inactive. Setting this bit disables this behavior.
When Keep Alive is active, any incoming real data will be pulled from the XCLK FIFO but not transmitted to ensure a clean FIFO once Keep Alive goes back to inactive.
When Keep Alive is active, no pulling of real data from the XCLK FIFO will occur.

@attributes.Name: Disable Keep Alive Wait For Samples

Description.#text: By default, when Keep Alive is active and the AUD driver has prepared the stream for real playback, but real samples have not yet arrived, HW will continue sending Keep Alive data until real samples do arrive. Setting this bit disables this waiting for samples behavior.
Keep Alive data will continue to be sent even after AUD driver has set the DPn_ChannelEnable Soundwire Classic register to a non-zero value, until the first real sample arrives.
Keep Alive data will stop once the AUD driver has set the DPn_ChannelEnable Soundwire Classic register to a non-zero value.

@attributes.Name: Disable Keep Alive Link Off Generation

Description.#text: Setting this bit disables Keep Alive output while the Soundwire link is off, and allows corresponding units to be clock gated when in the PS3 state.
Keep Alive operation will be maintained while the Soundwire link is off.
Keep Alive operation will be disabled when the Soundwire link is off.
Setting this bit disables Keep Alive output regardless of the SDCA Keep Alive register settings for usage during debugs.
Keep Alive will be enabled or disabled as normal based on the SDCA Keep Alive register settings.
Keep Alive is disabled regardless of the SDCA Keep Alive register settings.

This register provides controls for Refclk usage in Keep Alive streaming, as well as for timestamp generation while the Soundwire link is off. Setting this bit enables the usage of the custom M and N values written for each "DDA Index" through the AUD_SDW_REFCLK_M and AUD_SDW_REFCLK_N registers, instead of HW defaults. Normally, when the CMTG is being enabled after a DC6 state, it will wait for the transcoder to advertise that the Link and the TG are both up before starting its TG. When exiting DC6 with PR ALPM, the Link will not be up, so the CMTG will need to ignore that information.

This bit controls how the CMTG starts when being restored.

Normally, when the CMTG is being enabled through a mode-set, the CMTG will start at the end of the V. Active region.  However, when the CMTG is being restored from a DC6 state where power was removed, the CMTG may need to start at an earlier point to correctly align itself with the Port TG.  For example, if the set context latency (SCL) is positioned within V. Active then the CMTG will need to start at the start of the SCL window.

p.#text: HDMI/DVI: CRC is calculated on all pixels and blanking. The lane carrying the clock is replaced with all 0s. The first CRC done indication after CRC is first enabled is from a full frame and will have the expected CRC result. Subsequent CRC done indications will give a steady CRC result.

DisplayPort 1.x SST: CRC is calculated on all symbols. CRC sync point is the SR. CRC will start the clock after SR and end at the next SR (inclusive). Unused lanes are filled with zeroes when the port width is less than the number of available lanes. DDI_DFT DP_SR_once_a_frame should be enabled to get a deterministic result. The first CRC done indication after CRC is first enabled is from a full frame and will have the expected CRC result. Subsequent CRC done indications will give a steady CRC result. The SRD (PSR) CRC is taken on PSR entry, so the CRC needs to be enabled before PSR is entered. SST transcoder CRC cannot work with Enhanced Framing enabled.

DisplayPort 1.x MST: CRC is calculated on all symbols. CRC sync point is the SR. CRC will start the clock after SR and end at the next SR (inclusive). Unused lanes are filled with zeroes when the port width is less than the number of available lanes. DDI_DFT DP_SR_once_a_frame should be enabled to get a deterministic result. TRANS_DPT_PAT should be enabled to get a deterministic result. The first CRC done indication after CRC is first enabled is from a full frame and will have the expected CRC result. Subsequent CRC done indications will give a steady CRC result. The CRC done indications immediately after adding/deleting streams or forcing ACT will give differing, but deterministic results. Subsequent CRC done indications will give a steady CRC result. When compression is enabled with MST, TRANS_DPCOMP_DEBUG Port CRC in Compress Mode should be enabled to get a deterministic result.

In this mode the CRC engine will begin/end signature accumulation based on the frame count, start frame, and end frame values. p.#text: packetizer DTF DVP packet stream ctrl register

CaptureMask Specifies which BLB outputs will contribute to the new data value detection function. Each set bit corresponds to a input byte/BLB output pairing within this packetizerspanning up to 16 input byte lanes. The BLB outputs corresponding to masked in bits are combined based on the Capture Mode field to gate /ungate the data value change detection logic.
0: Means corresponding BLB output is not used for new data

If CaptureMode = 0 (AND mode), then Pktzr[0] will only store new data values if Pktzr[1].BLB[0] is true (see Section 2.3.1.2 for more

Trigger latency adjustment Specifies the trigger latency adjustment pipeline stage (if present in the RTL) to drive the input to the packet stream logic in order to account for fixed trigger logic latency from event recognizer output to Active/trigger input. The maximum number of additional pipeline stages is defined by the NUMLATSTAGES parameter, 0 , NUMLATSTAGES greater than or = 7. The latency adjustment pipeline is enabled on all DTF DVP clock cycles and is assumed to be the same clock driving trigger sequencer logic.

TriggerMode0 is Trigger logic mode to specify how the BLB outputs that are specified in the per byte-lane fields are combined to set the dtf_event_rec_out_0 signal for this packetizer.

ForceCaptureEn When set to '1, enables functionality to force a capture for this packetizer based on the dvp_force_capture input signal. When set to '0, the DVP ignores the value of the input signal.

CaptureMode, Capture qualifier logic mode to specify how the BLB outputs that are specified in the Capture Mask field are combined to influence the new data value detection logic. Rising edges of the capture qualifier output will cause the current data value to be captured regardless of whether it has changed since the previous DTF DVP clock. Subsequent DTF DVP clock cycles with capture qualifier logic asserted enables data value change detection logic until the capture qualifier logic output is deasserted.
01: All masked in BLB outputs are ORed together and data value change detection logic is enabled whenever any masked in BLB output is asserted

p.#text: PRE_CSC_CC2_GAMC_INDEX and PRE_CSC_CC2_GAMC_DATA registers are used to program the values that determine the characteristics of the gamma correction for the pipe pixel data before Color Space Conversion. Additional gamma correction can be done after the Color Space Conversion, if needed.
The gamma correction curve is represented by specifying a set of gamma entry reference points spaced equally along the curve for values between -1 and 1.

For input values greater than or equal to 0 and less than 1.0, the input value is used to linearly interpolate between two adjacent points of the 129 gamma entries to create the result value. The first 128 entries are stored as 24 bits per color in an unsigned 0.24 format with 0 integer and 24 fractional. The 129th entry is stored as 25 bits per color in a signed 1.24 format with 1 integer and 24 fractional bits.

For negative input values, gamma is mirrored along the X-axis, giving the same result as positive input values, except for a negative sign. When gamma input may be negative, the first gamma point should be programmed to a value of 0.0 in order to have a symmetric mirroring.

Pre CSC CC2 Gamma correction gets enabled or disabled based on the "Pipe Pre CSC CC2 Gamma Enable" bit in the GAMMA_MODE register. The same set of values is used for gamma correction of the red, blue and green channels.
See Pipe Gamma for an example gamma curve diagram.

p.#text: PRE_CSC_GAMC_INDEX and PRE_CSC_GAMC_DATA registers are used to program the values that determine the characteristics of the gamma correction for the pipe pixel data before Color Space Conversion. Additional gamma correction can be done after the Color Space Conversion Gamma if desired.

The gamma correction curve is represented by specifying a set of gamma entry reference points spaced equally along the curve for values between -1 and 1. For extended values there are extended gamma entry reference points. All input values are clamped to the greater than -7.0 and less than 7.0 range before the gamma calculation.

For input values greater than or equal to 0 and less than 1.0, the input value is used to linearly interpolate between two adjacent points of the first 129 gamma entries to create the result value. The first 128 entries are stored as 24 bits per color in an unsigned 0.24 format with 0 integer and 24 fractional. The 129
For input values greater than or equal to 1.0 and less than 3.0, the input value is used to linearly interpolate between the 129
For input values greater than or equal to 3.0 and less than 7.0, the input value is used to linearly interpolate between the 130

For negative input values, gamma is mirrored along the X-axis, giving the same result as positive input values, except for a negative sign. When gamma input may be negative, the first gamma point should be programmed to a value of 0.0 in order to have a symmetric mirroring.

Pre-CSC Gamma correction gets enabled or disabled based on the "Pipe CSC Enable" bit in the PLANE_COLOR_CTL register. The same set of values is used for gamma correction of the red, blue and green channels.
See Pipe Gamma for an example gamma curve diagram.

See the render response message definition table to find the source event for each bit.
The render response message is sent from the display engine to the render command streamer (CS) or blitter command streamer (BCS). The message is used to inform CS and BCS of certain display events.
This register is used to control which render response message bits are masked or unmasked.
Unmasked bits will cause a render response message to be sent and will be reported in that message.
Masked bits will not be reported and will not cause a render response message to be sent.

Vertical blank events occur periodically while the associated display pipe timing generator is running and will be reported in a render response to CS or BCS (depending on DE_RR_DEST destination selection) if un-masked here.

Scanline events occur after they have been initiated through MMIO writes or LRI to the Display Load Scan Lines register. A scanline done event will be reported in a render response to CS if un-masked here and the Display Load Scanline source is CS. A scanline done event will be reported in a render response to BCS if un-masked here and the Display Load Scanline source is BCS.

Flip done events occur after they have been initiated through MI_DISPLAY_FLIP or MMIO write to plane surface address registers. A flip event will be reported in a render response to CS if un-masked here and the flip source is CS. A flip event will be reported in a render response to BCS if un-masked here and the flip source is BCS.

p.#text: This bit controls what the DSB engine does when finished with a state buffer program.
If this bit is cleared, then the engine will stop and wait for Software to update the Head/Tail pointers before it starts processing the next state buffer.
If this bit is set, then the engine will start to re-fetch the state buffer defined by the current Head/Tail pointers when it finishes with the current program.

Note that the DSB engine will not take any action on this bit if it is not currently processing a state buffer. I.e. When Software sets this bit on an idle DSB engine, it must then write to the Tail Pointer to start the reiteration process.
This bit controls when the DSB engine starts to fetch a state buffer from memory.
When cleared, then the DSB engine will start fetching the state buffer immediately after Software writes the Tail Pointer
When set, then the DSB engine will start fetching the state buffer only after it sees a rising edge of VBLANK following the write to the Tail Pointer.
SW cannot have both bits 27 and 28 set at the same time.
This bit controls when the DSB engine starts to fetch a state buffer from memory.

When set, then the DSB engine will start fetching the state buffer only when the scanline falls in the range defined in DSB_LINERANGE_PF register following the write to the Tail Pointer.
SW cannot have both bits 27 and 28 set at the same time.

p.#text: When this counter is enabled by programming bit 31 of this register, DSB will insert programmed number of dead clocks after every 8 back to back MMIO cycles. This is needed to take care of the clock crossing timing issues. Driver must ensure the cdclk/dotclock ratio to adjust the programming. Below is the formula to calculate the number of dead clock programming is as follows.
If (cdclk/dotclk) <= 1 then DSB MMIO dead clock count = default value
else if (cdclk/dotclk) > 1 then DSB MMIO dead clock count = 11 *ROUNDUP(cdclk/dotclk)
elseDSB MMIO dead clock count = default value
Note: if the results of the above calculations are greater than the maximum supported value, set to the maximum value of 0xFF

p.#text: This field overrides the compressed frame buffer stride.
Compressed buffer stride in cachelines = ceiling [(round_up_to_even(plane width in pixels) * 4 * 4) / (64 * compression limit factor)]
At least plane width = a value greater than or equal to the width of the plane.
Software may choose to use a greater value in order to handle cases where the plane width is changing from frame to frame.

Compression limit factor is either 1, 2 or 4 based on the FBC_CTL Compression Limit field. If the limit is 2:1, the compression limit factor to be used is 2.Ceiling function rounds up any non-integer value to next greater number. Example ceiling [0.3] = 1, ceiling[2.1] = 3, ceiling[4.8] = 5, ceiling[4] = 4.
DSM allocation in bytes = min(640, ceiling (plane height / 4))* Compressed buffer stride in cachelines * 64

Description.#text: The value in this register and the value in DMC_DBG_EXEC_TP are used together by Main DMC to track the execution time of the associated program. If the value in this register and in the DMC_DBG_EXEC_TP register are 0x00000000, then Main DMC will report the execution time of the current/last program executed.

A value of 1 indicates that the Main DMC is currently executing and the value in the Execution Time field will reflect the current time since the start of execution. A value of 0 indicates that the Main DMC has completed execution and that the value in the Execution Time field is the time that Main DMC took to complete the program execution.

Software must ensure that the state buffer programming has a Frame Start opcode within it if this bit is set
If this bit is not set and the state buffer program contains a Frame Start opcode, the DSB engine will treat the opcode as a no-op
If this bit is set and Frame Start Opcode is not included in the DSB program then HW frame start will be used. There is not overriding to the HW frame start.

p.#text: This bit controls what the DSB engine does when finished with a state buffer program.
If this bit is cleared, then the engine will stop and wait for Software to update the Head/Tail pointers before it starts processing the next state buffer.
If this bit is set, then the engine will start to re-fetch the state buffer defined by the current Head/Tail pointers when it finishes with the current program.

Note that the DSB engine will not take any action on this bit if it is not currently processing a state buffer. I.e. When Software sets this bit on an idle DSB engine, it must then write to the Tail Pointer to start the reiteration process.
This bit controls when the DSB engine starts to fetch a state buffer from memory.
When cleared, then the DSB engine will start fetching the state buffer immediately after Software writes the Tail Pointer
When set, then the DSB engine will start fetching the state buffer only after it sees a rising edge of VBLANK following the write to the Tail Pointer.
SW cannot have both bits 27 and 28 set at the same time.
This bit controls when the DSB engine starts to fetch a state buffer from memory.
When cleared, then the DSB engine will start fetching the state buffer immediately after Software writes the Tail Pointer
When set, then the DSB engine will start fetching the state buffer only when the scanline falls in the range defined in DSB_LINERANGE_PF register following the write to the Tail Pointer.
SW cannot have both bits 27 and 28 set at the same time.

p.#text: Access: Sent from GT to North Display
This message is used to initiate a display scan line compare.
This command streamer message driven scan line compare can not be used at the same time as the MMIO driven scan line compare on the same pipe.

When this message is received, the Display Engine (DE) will start comparing the display pipe timing generator or plane (selectable) current scan line value (current scan line) with the start scan line value (current scan line >= start scan line) and the end scan line value (current scan line <= end scan line) to decide if the pipe scan line is inside or outside the scan line window of interest. DE will wait until the current scan line is either outside (Inclusive mode) or inside (Exclusive mode) the scan line window, then trigger a scan line event and stop any further comparing.
A new scan line compare must not be started until after the previous compare has finished.

The scan line event can cause display to send a scan line compare response to the render command streamer, used for releasing a MI_WAIT_FOR_EVENT on scan line window, if unmasked in the DERRMR mask register 0x44050. The scan line event can also cause display to generate a scan line compare interrupt, if unmasked and enabled in the DEIMR and DEIER display engine interrupt registers.

The end scan line value must be greater than or equal to the start scan line value. The value programmed should be the desired value - 1, so for scan line 0, the value programmed is vertical total, and for scan line 1, the value programmed is 0.
In interlaced display timings, the current scan line is thecurrent line of the current interlaced field.
Either MMIO or a MI_LOAD_REGISTER_IMM command can be used to unmask the scan line render response 0x44050.

A turnaround delay is needed to ensure that there is adequate time for DE to observe the de-assertion of PICA’s grant after receiving DE’s write data bits or read address bits before PICA asserts the grant (overloaded to be request) when sending the completion.

So the defalault value is 128 sideband clock cycles.

p.#text: This register defines the number of excess pixels within the Pipe window (on the right or left) that the Scaler will need to remove from the post scaled image.

When an image is split across two Pipes, scaled, and then joined at the Port, the Scalers within each Pipe will operate on a splitimage that contains overlap pixels around where the final seam will be to facilitate a seamless join at the Port. For example, if the left portion of an image is being scaled in Pipe A and the right portion of the image is being scaled in Pipe B, then there will be an excess number of pixels (i.e. overlap pixels) on the right side of the Pipe A image and an excess number of pixels on the left side of the Pipe B image. The overlap pixels of the window within each of the Pipes need to be dropped by the Scaler before they are delivered to the Port.

li.#text: Dropping of the overlap/excess pixels is done at the very end of the Pipe within the Scaler regardless of whether a Scaler is bound to the Pipe, or not.

The number of excess pixels cannot exceed the size of the horizontal blank, otherwise there will not be enough time to throw them away before starting the next line and the image will be corrupted

p.#text: This bit enables the DSB engine.
Notes:

li.#text: The act of enabling the DSB engine will not result in the engine to start fetching a state buffer from memory. Only a write to the Tail Pointer will start a fetch
A write to the Tail Pointer of the DSB engine will have no affect if the DSB engine is not enabled
SW should not update the DSB control registers while DSB engine is not in IDLE state. Bit 0 indicates the status of DSB engine.
If SW desires to reset the DSB engine then following sequence can be followed. This sequence is also described in the DSB programming details (TBD)
To reset the DSB engine, SW can set this bit to 0. Bit31 transition from 1 to 0 initiates a reset sequence in the DSB HW.
Poll for the DSB status (bit 0) to be in IDLE.
If DSB status is 0 then the DSB engine reset sequence is complete and DSB is in reset state.

Description.#text: This bit controls whether this DSB is going to generate the frame start for the pipe

li.#text: Only one DSB engine within a given pipe can have this bit set. Undesirable behavor will result if more than one DSB is generating a frame start to the pipe.
Software must ensure that the state buffer programming has a Frame Start opcode within it if this bit is set
If this bit is not set and the state buffer program contains a Frame Start opcode, the DSB engine will treat the opcode as a no-op
If this bit is set and Frame Start Opcode is not included in the DSB program then HW frame start will be used. There is not overriding to the HW frame start.

p.#text: This bit controls what the DSB engine does when finished with a state buffer program.
If this bit is cleared, then the engine will stop and wait for Software to update the Head/Tail pointers before it starts processing the next state buffer.
If this bit is set, then the engine will start to re-fetch the state buffer defined by the current Head/Tail pointers when it finishes with the current program.

Note that the DSB engine will not take any action on this bit if it is not currently processing a state buffer. I.e. When Software sets this bit on an idle DSB engine, it must then write to the Tail Pointer to start the reiteration process.
This bit controls when the DSB engine starts to fetch a state buffer from memory.
When cleared, then the DSB engine will start fetching the state buffer immediately after Software writes the Tail Pointer
When set, then the DSB engine will start fetching the state buffer only after it sees a rising edge of VBLANK following the write to the Tail Pointer.
SW cannot have both bits 27 and 28 set at the same time.
This bit controls when the DSB engine starts to fetch a state buffer from memory.
When cleared, then the DSB engine will start fetching the state buffer immediately after Software writes the Tail Pointer
When set, then the DSB engine will start fetching the state buffer only when the scanline falls in the range defined in DSB_LINERANGE_PF register following the write to the Tail Pointer.
SW cannot have both bits 27 and 28 set at the same time.

p.#text: CUR_PRE_CSC_GAMC_INDEX and CUR_PRE_CSC_GAMC_DATA registers are used to program the values that determine the characteristics of the gamma correction for the cursor pixel data before Color Space Conversion. Additional gamma correction can be done after the Color Space Conversion if desired.

The gamma correction curve is represented by specifying a set of gamma entry reference points spaced equally along the curve for values between -1 and 1. For extended values there are extended gamma entry reference points. All input values are clamped to the greater than -7.0 and less than 7.0 range before the gamma calculation.

For input values greater than or equal to 0 and less than 1.0, the input value is used to linearly interpolate between two adjacent points of the first 33 gamma entries to create the result value. The first 32 entries are stored as 16 bits per color in an unsigned 0.16 format with 0 integer and 16 fractional. The 33
For input values greater than or equal to 1.0 and less than 3.0, the input value is used to linearly interpolate between the 33
For input values greater than or equal to 3.0 and less than 7.0, the input value is used to linearly interpolate between the 34

For negative input values, gamma is mirrored along the X-axis, giving the same result as positive input values, except for a negative sign. When gamma input may be negative, the first gamma point should be programmed to a value of 0.0 in order to have a symmetric mirroring.
Pre-CSC Gamma correction gets enabled or disabled based on the "Pre CSC Enable" bit in the CUR_CTL register.

li.#text: The maximum horizontal plane size allowed is 4096 pixels

p.#text: The maximum horizontal plane size allowed is 4096 pixels with even panning and 4095 with odd panning when the Chroma upsampler is enabled.

When the horizontal plane size is not a multiple of 4, then the number of UV components delivered to the CUS will be odd. The CUS HW is able to handle this, but during simulation the Plane feeding the CUS may deliver an X on the last slot of the UV component transfer at the end of the UV line (assuming a 2 pixel per clock interface). The X within the incoming data will corrupt the ECC calculated for the SSA write data (ECC will propagate the X), and when reading the UV components from the SSA, the ECC decode will corrupt the full read payload which propagates the X onto the final good UV component.
Options to handle this:

Note that this is a simulation pessimism issue only. In silicon, the upper UV component on the last data transfer will have a known value (it will be a random value, but there is no concept of an X in Si) which will generate a valid ECC for the SSA write data.

li.#text: When the horizontal plane size is not a multiple of 4, then the simulation environment can disable ECC (i.e. set the ECC Bypass bit of this register). This will prevent the X on the "dummy" UV component from propagating through the ECC and onto the last valid UV component.
Ensure that thehorizontal plane size is restricted to a multiple of 4. This will ensure there are an even number of UV components delivered to the CUS.

p.#text: PLANE_POST_CSC_GAMC_INDEX and PLANE_POST_CSC_GAMC_DATA registers are used to program the values that determine the characteristics of the gamma correction for the plane pixel data after plane Color Space Conversion.

The gamma correction curve is represented by specifying a set of gamma entry reference points spaced equally along the curve for values between -1 and 1. For extended values there are extended gamma entry reference points. All input values are clamped to the greater than -7.0 and less than 7.0 range before the gamma calculation.

For input values greater than or equal to 0 and less than 1.0, the input value is used to linearly interpolate between two adjacent points of the first 33 gamma entries to create the result value. The first 32 entries are stored as 16 bits per color in an unsigned 0.16 format with 0 integer and16 fractional. The 33
For input values greater than or equal to 1.0 and less than 3.0, the input value is used to linearly interpolate between the 33
For input values greater than or equal to 3.0 and less than 7.0, the input value is used to linearly interpolate between the 34

For negative input values, gamma is mirrored along the X-axis, giving the same result as positive input values, except for a negative sign. When gamma input may be negative, the first gamma point should be programmed to a value of 0.0 in order to have a symmetric mirroring.

Plane Post-CSC Gamma correction gets enabled or disabled based on the 'Plane Gamma Disable' bit in the 'PLANE_COLOR_CTL' register. The same set of values is used for gamma correction of the red, blue and green channels.

Additional gamma correction can be done after the Color Space Conversion, if needed.

The gamma correction curve is represented by specifying a set of gamma entry reference points spaced equally along the curve for values between -1 and 1. For extended values there are extended gamma entry reference points. All input values are clamped to the greater than -7.0 and less than 7.0 range before the gamma calculation.

For input values greater than or equal to 0 and less than 1.0, the input value is used to linearly interpolate between two adjacent points of the first 33 gamma entries to create the result value. The first 32 entries are stored as 24 bits per color in an unsigned 0.24 format with 0 integer and 24 fractional. The 33
For input values greater than or equal to 1.0 and less than 3.0, the input value is used to linearly interpolate between the 33
For input values greater than or equal to 3.0 and less than 7.0, the input value is used to linearly interpolate between the 34

For negative input values, gamma is mirrored along the X-axis, giving the same result as positive input values, except for a negative sign. When gamma input may be negative, the first gamma point should be programmed to a value of 0.0 in order to have a symmetric mirroring.

Pre-CSC Gamma correction gets enabled or disabled based on the "Pipe CSC Enable" bit in the plane control register. The same set of values is used for gamma correction of the red, blue and green channels.
See Pipe Gamma for an example gamma curve diagram.

To program the gamma correction entries, calculate the desired gamma curve for inputs from 0 to 7.0. For inputs of 0 to 1.0, multiply the input value by 32 to find the gamma entry number, then store the desired gamma result in that entry. For inputs greater than 1.0 and less than or equal to 3.0, store the result for an input of 3.0 in the 34

For HDR tone mapping usages, only the first 33 entries gets used. The entries are used either in an unsigned 0.24 format or unsigned 8.16 format based on PLANE_COLOR_CTL->Plane Gamma Multiplier Precision programming.

p.#text: Horizontal line number of the new surface after an async flip occurs. If the async flip occurs toward the end of the frame and the hardware converts the async flip to a sync flip, this field will indicate the value 0.
This field is not double buffered.
This field specifies the stride for the plane. The field is used to determine the line to line increment for the plane.
For Linear memory, this field specifies the stride in chunks of 64 bytes (1 cache line). Example: If the programmed value is 100, the stride = 100 * 64 = 6400 bytes.
For Tile 4 memory, this field specifies the stride in number of 128 byte wide tiles. Example: If the programmed value is 10, the stride = 10 * 128 = 1280 bytes.
For Tile X memory, this field specifies the stride in number of 512 byte wide tiles. Example: If the programmed value is 10, the stride = 10 * 512 = 5120 bytes.
For YUV planar (NV12 or P0xx) plane pixel formats, the stride calculated in bytes should be equal for the Y and UV surfaces.

The stride in bytes must not exceed 128K bytes. For pixel formats of 64bpp, the maximum stride in tiles as listed below, will allow for a 16K pixel surface. Adjustments to PLANE_OFFSET and PLANE_SURF allow panning across the surface.

This bit is only allowed to change on synchronous updates, but once set, the bit can remain set while using asynchronous updates.

This field enables asynchronous updates of the plane surface address (async flips). The surface address will change as soon as possible. This bit is not double buffered and the changes will apply immediately. When performing an asynchronous update, only the plane surface can be updated. Changes to stride, pixel, format, compression, FBC, etc. are not allowed.
Surface Address MMIO writes will update synchronous to start of vertical blank

There is one instance of this register for each plane.

p.#text: If this Plane is configured as the Back Plane of a Smooth Sync Plane pair (i.e. the Smooth Sync Plane Enable is set within the PLANE_CTL register of this Plane), and the Line Number Start Advertisement is enabled (offsets given below), then this register will reflect the last Line Number Start that this Plane sent to its Front Plane neighbor.

Note that the behavior of this field will remain unchanged (i.e. it will advertise the live surface base address) for the Back Plane if the Line Number Start Advertiesment is not enabled. Also, the behavior of this register for the Front Plane of a Smooth Sync pair remains unchanged regardless of the Line Number Start Advertisement setting.
The register to enable the Line Number Start advertisement is within each Plane with the following offset:
Pipe offset address [31:12] + Plane offset address [11:8] + Register offset address [8:0]
Where:

li.#text: Register offset address [8:0] = 16Ch
Plane offset address [11:8] = Plane number (e.g. 1 to 5)
Pipe offset address [31:12]
Pipe A = 70h
Pipe B = 71h
Pipe C = 72h
Pipe D = 73h
