p.#text: This register controls the advanced link power management (ALPM) functionality within the embedded DP transcoder
Overall programming notes:

li.#text: Except for the LOBF Enable and restore bits, the fields within this register shall only be changed when the PM functions (i.e. PSR1, PSR2, and Panel Replay) are disabled.
Software can change the LOBF Enable bit dynamically, but it cannot change any other fields within this register when LOBF is enabled

p.#text: This bit will select between PR with or without ALPM.
When PR is Enabled (TRANS_DP2_CTL) and:
This bit is ignored if PR is not enabled

li.#text: ALPM is Disabled, then PR will operate in DP mode (i.e. the main link will not be turned off)
ALPM is Enabled, then PR will operate in eDP mode (i.e. the main link will be turned off when idle)

p.#text: This bit will select between PR with or without ALPM.
When PR is Enabled (TRANS_DP2_CTL) and:
This bit is ignored if PR is not enabled

li.#text: ALPM is Disabled, then PR will operate in Link On mode (i.e. the main link will not be turned off)
ALPM is Enabled, then PR will operate in ALPM mode (i.e. the main link will be turned off when idle)

Description.#text: PR without ALPM (i.e. Link On)
PR with ALPM

p.#text: This field enables the AUX-less ALPM flows
Software is responsible for ensuring the following:

li.#text: The programming of this field must match the programming of the ALPM AUX-Less Enable within the PORT_ALPM_CTL register

p.#text: This field enables the transcoder to put the main link to sleep during the VRR Safe Window when PSR1, PSR2, and Panel Replay (PR) are disabled.

li.#text: Link Off Between Frames (LOBF) should not be enabled when PSR1, PSR2, or PR (with or without ALPM) are enabled
LOBF cannot be enabled if the Safe Window is not greater than the ALPM Entry Check
LOBF cannot be enabled if the number of lines from the start of the Set Context Latency window to the first SDP transmission line (TL) is not greater than the "Wake Time"
The location of the first SDP TL
If EMP_AS_SDP_TL <= VRRGuardband, then the first SDP TL is the first line of the VRR Guardband window
If EMP_AS_SDP_TL > VRR Guardband, then the first SDP TL = (VTOTAL - EMP_AS_SDP_TL)
The Wake Time
If the AUX-Wake flows are enabled (ALPM AUX-Less Enable = 0), then Wake Time = PSR2_CTL[ IO Buffer Wake ]
Otherwise (ALPM AUX-Less Enable = 1), then Wake Time = ALPM_CTL[ AUX-Less Wake Time ]

Description.#text: PSR2_CTL[ Fast Wake ] used for non-PSR1 AUX-Wake flows
ALPM_CTL[ Extended Fast Wake Time ] used fornon-PSR1 AUX-Wake flows

p.#text: This bit allows the ALPM block to use the Extended Fast Wake Time for the AUX-Wake flows that send the Fast Wake request over AUX.

Software should enable this when using the AUX-Wake flows (ALPM AUX-Less Enable = 0). If the extended fast wake is not enabled, then the ALPM block will use the PSR2_CTL[ Fast Wake ] field to determine when to send the AUX Fast Wake to the Sink (that field is limited to 12 lines).
This bit is ignored when the AUX-Less flows are enabled, or PSR1 is enabled

@attributes.Name: Keep FEC Enabled for AUX-Wake Sleep

p.#text: The AUX-Wake operation does not require FEC to remain enabled during the SLEEP flow, so the legacy behavior of the transcoder has been to disable FEC when entering the SLEEP flow.
The AUX-Less operation requires FEC to remain enabled during the SLEEP flow.
This bit will allow the transcoder to apply the AUX-Less FEC policy to the AUX-Wake SLEEP flow.
This bit indicates that the transcoder has been restored from a Sleep or Deep Sleep state at some point in the past.
Hardware will set this bit when the DMC clears either of the "Restore to *" bits within this register (i.e. the DMC has completed a restore).
Software will clear this bit when it is looking for the transcoder to have exited a low power state (DC6/DC6v).
This bit indicates whether a restore has occurred where the main link was OFF before the DMC entered a DC6/DC6vstate.
The DMC should set this bit when there is a:

li.#text: PSR1 restore
PSR2 restore from DC6v
PR with ALPM restore
Restore from DC6v where PSR*/PR are not enabled (i.e. Link Off Between Frames)
This field is used for hardware communication. Software must not change this field.
At a minimum, the DMC shall program this bit before it enables the DDI Function (i.e. before restoring any of the transcoder registers)
The DMC shall clear this bit after it has Enabled the Transcoder (i.e. after restoring all of the transcoder registers)

p.#text: The DMC will set this bit to indicate that the transcoder has been restored from DC6 while PSR2 was enabled and the main link was OFF before entering DC6.

li.#text: This field is used for hardware communication. Software must not change this field.
At a minimum, the DMC shall program this bit before it enables the DDI Function (i.e. before restoring any of the transcoder registers)
The DMC shall clear this bit after it has Enabled the Transcoder (i.e. after restoring all of the transcoder registers)

Description.#text: Minimum hold time
This field specifies the number of zeroes the Source should transmit after the last ML_PHY_SLEEP sequence when doing an AUX-less Fast Sleep
Minimum per eDP 1.5 specification
This field specifies the number of zeroes the Source should transmit after the last ML_PHY_SLEEP sequence when doing an AUX-less Fast Sleep
Transcoder will only transmit ML_PHY_SLEEP sequences
Transcoder will transmit zeroes after 4 ML_PHY_SLEEP sequences

p.#text: When enabled, the transcoder will mimic the AUX-Less sleep flow by appending scrambled zeroes after the 4 ML_PHY_SLEEP sequences have been transmitted (a minimum of 4 ML_PHY_SLEEP sequences are required).The ALPM block will use the "AUX Less Sleep Hold Time" programming to determine how many zeroes to send after the ML_PHY_SLEEP sequences.
If this is not enabled, then the transcoder will continue to transmit ML_PHY_SLEEP sequences after the minimum 4 sequences have been transmitted.

This field represents the number of lines needed to put the main link to sleep and keep it in the sleep state before it can be taken out of the SLEEP state (eDP requires the main link to be in the SLEEP state for a minimum of 5us).
Hardware will use this to check if it has enough time to put the main link to sleep when in the following modes of operation:

li.#text: When there are no other power management features (i.e. PSR, PSR2, or PR) are enabled, but ALPM is enabled (i.e. link off between active frames). If there are enough lines within the Safe Window to allow the main link to be put to sleep, then the transcoder will do this.

When PR with ALPM and AS SDP's are enabled the PR logic will determine if it can put the main link to sleep at the end of a capture frame / selective update region. If the AS SDP has to be transmitted in T1, it's possible the time between putting the main link to sleep and waking it back up would violate the eDP requirements. If PR cannot put the main link to SLEEP, then it will keep the main link ON, but will be transmitting "dummy data"

When PSR2 is enabled, the PSR2 logic will determine if it can put the main link to sleep at the end of a capture frame if there is going to be a Selective Update in the next frame (i.e. from the CRC VSC SDP to the start of the next SU).

Hardware will use this to check if it has enough time to put the main link to sleep when in the following modes of operation:

When PR with ALPM and AS SDP's are enabled the PR logic will determine if it can put the main link to sleep at the end of a capture frame / selective update region. If the AS SDP has to be transmitted in T1, it's possible the time between putting the main link to sleep and waking it back up would violate the eDP requirements. If PR cannot put the main link to SLEEP, then it will keep the main link ON, but will be transmitting "dummy data"

When PSR2 is enabled, the PSR2 logic will determine if it can put the main link to sleep at the end of a capture frame if there is going to be a Selective Update in the next frame (i.e. from the CRC VSC SDP to the start of the next SU).

p.#text: This bit indicates to the transcoder when the DMC is using the DC3 clock off (DC3co) low power mechanism.

From the transcoder's perspective, it will be operating in a DC6v mode when the DMC is using the DC3 clock off low power mechanism. For the most part DC6v vs. DC3co is completely transparent to the transcoder except for how the transcoder advertises idleness to the DMC in PR ALPM with AS SDP transmissions enabled.
Notes:

li.#text: In DC6v the transcoder will need to de-assert its Idle when there is a pending AS SDP transmission within a given V. Blank region to prevent the DMC going back to DC6v before the packet is transmitted.
In DC3co the transcoder can keep its Idle asserted when there is a pending AS SDP transmission since there is no information it needs from the CD clock domain to transmit the packet.
This bit only affects the behavior of the Transcoder Idle when PR ALPM is Active, AS SDPs are enabled (VIDEO_DIP_CTL), and AS SDP transmission in PR Active is enabled (this register).

If the transcoder is allowed to put the ML to sleep, then it will determine if there is enough time between the AS SDP and the SU to put the ML to sleep and bring it back up in time for the SU start. If it determines there is not enough time, then it will keep the ML awake.

When PSR2 is in the Deep Sleep state, the transcoder's timing generator is off, and the Main Link is off (the Link Status should reflect this)

When PSR2 is exiting the Deep Sleep state (i.e. it is waking up the Main Link and turning on the timing generator), it will end up in the Inactive state - PSR2 Deep Sleep -> PSR2 Deep Sleep Exit -> PSR2 Inactive. There is no other path from the Deep Sleep state.

Transisions out of the CAPTURE FRAME state and transitions into the DEEP SLEEP state are done at an internal "Frame Marker" point which happens after entering the delayed vblank.  In addition to this delay there is delay due to clock crossing the information from the transcoders clock domain to this register. If SW is checking this field based off something that is anchored to the entry of the delayed vblank, then it needs to comprehend this delay (i.e. SW should wait for at least one line time after the entry of the delayed vblank to allow hardware to reach the Frame Marker and clock cross the information to this register).

The duration that the hardware stays in some of these states is non-deterministic, so SW may not see all of the state transitions when reading this field. SW must comprehend this if it is doing explicit state checks.

p.#text: This field selects the scaler type which determines the precision that the scaler processes pixels at.

When operating in the non-linear mode and the scaler is bound to a pixel source that can deliver linear pixels (e.g. HDR planes, linear pipe tap), the scaler will only process the most significant non-linear portion of the incoming pixels (the lower bits of each channel are simply dropped). A loss of precision will occur if the pixel values are more significant than a non-linear precision (i.e. the lowerbits are non-zero) which can lead to "banding"

When operating in the linear mode, the scaler will process the full linear precision of the incoming pixels (only possible for HDR panes or at the linear pipe tap), but the scaler will compress the pixels when writing into its line buffers (line buffers can only store non-linear precision) and de-compress back to a full linear precision when reading the pixels out of the line buffers.

li.#text: Non-linear: Scales using non-linear pixel precision
Linear: Scales using linear pixel precision

(SW_CLR_INT) This bit must be clear for normal operation. Setting the bit then clearing it acts as local reset to the GMBUS controller. This bit is commonly used by software to clear a BUS_ERROR when a slave device delivers a NACK.

When the SW_CLR_INT bit is asserted, all writes to the GMBUS2, GMBUS3, and GMBUS4 registers are discarded. The GMBUS1 register writes to any other bit except the SW_CLR_INT are also lost. Reads to these registers always work normally regardless of the state of the SW_CLR_INT bit.

(SW_CLR_INT) This bit must be clear for normal operation. Setting the bit then clearing it acts as local reset to the GMBUS controller. This bit is commonly used by software to clear a BUS_ERROR when a secondary device delivers a NACK.

When the SW_CLR_INT bit is asserted, all writes to the GPIO and GMBUS registers are discarded. The GMBUS1 register writes to any other bit except the SW_CLR_INT are also lost. Reads to these registers always work normally regardless of the state of the SW_CLR_INT bit.

p.#text: GMBUS cycle will always consist of a START followed by Slave Address, followed by an optional read or write data phase. A read cycle with an index will consist of a START followed by a Slave Address a WRITE indication and the INDEX and then a RESTART with a Slave Address and an optional read data phase. The GMBUS cycle will terminate either with a STOP or by entering a wait state. The WAIT state is exited by generating a STOP or by starting another GMBUS cycle. This can only cause a STOP to be generated if a GMBUS cycle is generated, the GMBUS is currently in a data phase, or it is in a WAIT phase.
The three bits can be decoded as follows:
27 = STOP generated
26 = INDEX used
25 = Cycle ends in a WAIT

GMBUS cycle will always consist of a START followed by Secondary Address, followed by an optional read or write data phase. A read cycle with an index will consist of a START followed by a Secondary Address a WRITE indication and the INDEX and then a RESTART with a Secondary Address and an optional read data phase. The GMBUS cycle will terminate either with a STOP or by entering a wait state. The WAIT state is exited by generating a STOP or by starting another GMBUS cycle. This can only cause a STOP to be generated if a GMBUS cycle is generated, the GMBUS is currently in a data phase, or it is in a WAIT phase.
The three bits can be decoded as follows:
27 = STOP generated
26 = INDEX used
25 = Cycle ends in a WAIT

Description.#text: No GMBUS cycle is generated
GMBUS cycle is generated without an INDEX, with no STOP, and ends with a WAIT
Reserved
GMBUS cycle is generated with an INDEX, with no STOP, and ends with a WAIT
Generates a STOP if currently in a WAIT or after the completion of the current byte if active
GMBUS cycle is generated without an INDEX and with a STOP
Reserved
GMBUS cycle is generated with an INDEX and with a STOP

This determines the total number of bytes to be transferred during the DATA phase of a GMBUS cycle. The DATA phase can be prematurely terminated by generating a STOP while in the DATA phase (see Bus Cycle Select).

p.#text: (INDEX) This field specifies the 8-bits of index to be used for the generated bus write transaction or the index used for the WRITE portion of the WRITE/READ pair. It only has an effect if the enable Index bit is set.
This field may be referred to as "8 bit Secondary Register Index"

Description.#text: (INDEX) This field specifies the 8-bits of index to be used for the generated bus write transaction or the index used for the WRITE portion of the WRITE/READ pair. It only has an effect if the enable Index bit is set.

p.#text: Bits 7:1 = 7-bit GMBUS Slave Address (SADDR): When a GMBUS cycle is to be generated using the Bus Cycle Select field, this field specifies the value of the slave address that is to be sent out. For use with 10-bit slave address devices, set this value to 11110XXb (where the last two bits (XX) are the two MSBs of the 10-bit address) and the slave direction bit to a write. This is followed by the first data byte being the 8 LSBs of the 10-bit slave address.

Bit 0 = Slave Direction Bit: When a GMBUS cycle is to be generated based on the Bus Cycle Select, this bit determines if the operation will be a read or a write. A read operation with the index enabled will perform a write with just the index followed by a re-start and a read. A 1 indicates that a Read from the slave device operation is to be performed. A 0 indicates that a Write to the slave device operation is to be performed.
This field may be referred to as "Secondary Address And Direction"

Bits 7:1 = 7-bit GMBUS Secondary Address (SADDR): When a GMBUS cycle is to be generated using the Bus Cycle Select field, this field specifies the value of the secondary address that is to be sent out. For use with 10-bit secondary address devices, set this value to 11110XXb (where the last two bits (XX) are the two MSBs of the 10-bit address) and the secondary direction bit to a write. This is followed by the first data byte being the 8 LSBs of the 10-bit secondary address.

Bit 0 = Secondary Direction Bit: When a GMBUS cycle is to be generated based on the Bus Cycle Select, this bit determines if the operation will be a read or a write. A read operation with the index enabled will perform a write with just the index followed by a re-start and a read. A 1 indicates that a Read from the secondary device operation is to be performed. A 0 indicates that a Write to the secondary device operation is to be performed.

Description.#text: When the SW_CLR_INT bit is asserted, all writes to this register are discarded. Reads to this register always work normally regardless of the state of the SW_CLR_INT bit.

Software wishing to arbitrate for the GMBUS resource can poll this bit until it reads a zero and will then own usage of the GMBUS controller. This bit has no effect on the hardware, and is only used as semaphore among various independent software threads.Writing a one to this bit is software's indication that the software use of this resource is now terminated and it is available for other clients.

Read operation that contains a zero in this bit position indicates that the GMBUS engine is now acquired and the subsequent reads of this register will now have this bit set. Writing a 0 to this bit has no effect.

Read operation that contains a one for this bit indicates that the GMBUS is currently allocated to someone else and "In use". Once set, a write of a 1 to this bit indicates that the software has relinquished the GMBUS resource and will reset the value of this bit to a 0.

Once in a WAIT_PHASE, the software can now choose to generate a STOP cycle or a repeated start (RESTART) cycle followed by another GMBUS transaction.Wait phase is entered at the end of the current transaction when that transaction is selected not to terminate with a STOP.

(HW_RDY) This provides a method of detecting when the current software client routine can proceed with the next step in a sequence of GMBUS operations. This data handshake bit is used in conjunction with the SW_RDY bit. When this bit is asserted by the GMBUS controller, it results in the de-assertion of the SW_RDY bit.This bit resumes to normal operation when the SW_CLR_INT bit is written to a 0.

Condition required for assertion has not occurred or when this bit is a one and:- SW_RDY bit has been asserted- During a GMBUS read transaction, after the each read of the data register- During a GMBUS write transaction, after each write of the data register- SW_CLR_INT bit has been cleared

This bit is asserted under the following conditions: - After a reset or when the transaction is aborted by the setting of the SW_CLR_INT bit - When an active GMBUS cycle has terminated with a STOP - When during a GMBUS write transaction, the data register needs and can accept another four bytes of data - During a GMBUS read transaction, this bit is asserted when the data register has four bytes of new data or the read transaction DATA phase is complete and the data register contains the last few bytes of the read data

(GA) This is a status bit that indicates whether the GMBUS controller is in an IDLE state or not.  Active states are the START, ADDRESS, INDEX, DATA, WAIT, or STOP Phase.

Can be used to determine the number of bytes currently transmitted/received by the GMBUS controller hardware. Hardware sets it to zero at the start of a GMBUS transaction data transfer and incremented after the completion of each byte of the data phase. Note that because reads have internal storage, the byte count on a read operation may be ahead of the data that has been accepted from the data register.

Data is transferred with the most significant bit of the least significant byte first.

For GMBUS write operations with a non-zero byte count, this register should be written with the data before the GMBUS cycle is initiated. For byte counts that are greater than four bytes, this register will be written with subsequent data only after the HW_RDY status bit is set indicating that the register is now ready for additional data. For GMBUS read operations, software should wait until the HW_RDY bit indicates that the register contains the next set of valid read data before reading this register.

This field specifies which GMBUS interrupts events may contribute to the setting of GMBUS interrupt status bit in the second level interrupt status register.For writes, the HW Ready (HWRDY) interrupt indicates that software can write the next DWORD. It does NOT mean that the transfer of data to the slave device has completed. The IDLE or HW wait interrupt may be used to detect the end of writing data to the slave device. The HWRDY interrupt may be used for gmbus write cycles only to detect when to write the next DWORD after the first two DWORDs have been written to GMBUS3. For reads, the HWRDY interrupt indicates the arrival of the next dword.

This field specifies which GMBUS interrupts events may contribute to the setting of GMBUS interrupt status bit in the second level interrupt status register.For writes, the HW Ready (HWRDY) interrupt indicates that software can write the next DWORD. It does NOT mean that the transfer of data to the secondary device has completed. The IDLE or HW wait interrupt may be used to detect the end of writing data to the secondary device. The HWRDY interrupt may be used for gmbus write cycles only to detect when to write the next DWORD after the first two DWORDs have been written to GMBUS3. For reads, the HWRDY interrupt indicates the arrival of the next dword.

If enabled by the IER, bits set in this register will generate a south display interrupt. Bits set in this register will remain set (persist) until the interrupt condition is cleared by writing a '1' to the appropriate bits. For each bit, the IIR can store a second pending interrupt if two or more of the same interrupt conditions occur before the first condition is cleared. Upon clearing the interrupt, the IIR bit and south display interrupt will momentarily go low, then return high to indicate there is another interrupt pending.

These are the Interrupt Enable Register Bits. The field enables a south display interrupt to be generated whenever the corresponding bit in the IIR becomes set. A disabled interrupt will still appear in the IIR.

p.#text: This register defines the base transmission line for the following "common" DP/eDP SDP's
Programming Notes:

li.#text: Video Stream Configuration (VSC)
Gamut Metadata Packet (GMP)
Picture Parameter Set (PPS)
VSC Extension (VSC EXT)
This register specifies a fixed position from the end of the Vblank
All of the above SDPs (except for VSC) can be individually offset / staggered using CMN_SDP_TL_STGR_CT (<SDP Type> TL = (Vblank End - CMN_SDP_TL) + CMN_SDP_TL_STGR_CT[ <SDP Type> ])
The double buffering for these packets is handled within the transcoders and not within the register block itself
The double buffering is done in the transcoder clock domain (e.g. the symbol clock domain). This means that the packet data will be clock crossed before it is double buffered
The double buffering of the packet data is with respect to the final transmission line for the SDP type

To keep the clock crossing of the different SDP type registers atomic, Software should program the packet data first and the packet header last. The clock crossing of all register data will be triggered off of the header write
Software should ensure that the packet header write is done before the final transmission line for the given SDP type
The transmission line for each SDP type must not be within the V. Active region and should be positioned at least one line into the V. Blank

When Panel Replay and AS SDPs are enabled, the eDP/DP standard requires the VSC SDP indicating PR Active to be sent out before the AS SDP. Therefore, the following programming restriction is required for this configuration:
If PSR1 is going to be used with the Sink, then Software must position CMN_SDP_TL on the second line of the VRR Guardband (i.e. CMN_SDP_TL = (VRR Guardband-1))

p.#text: (V. Active + 1) <= (Vmin - SDP TL)
CMN_SDP_TL >= EMP_AS_SDP_TL
This bit enables the eDP/DP transcoder to use this register for the transmission line of the common SDPs (for backwards compatibility).
If this register is not enabled (the default) then:

li.#text: The transcoder will use the second line of delayed V. Blank as the base transmission line for all of the common SDPs (except for VSC SDPs).

p.#text: This register defines the offsets (i.e. stagger) of the specified SDP types with respect to the base transmission line as defined by CMN_SDP_TL.
The final transmission line of the given SDP will be:
(Vblank End - CMN_SDP_TL) + CMN_SDP_TL_STGR_CTL[ <SDP Type> ]
Note that some SDP types default to a non-zero staggering where the Valid Value indicates the default value. However, all encodings for all SDP types are valid.

li.#text: The stagger for a given SDP cannot be greater than the CMN_SDP_TL (CMN_SDP_TL >= CMN_SDP_TL_STGR_CTL[ <SDP Type> ])
If a given SDP type can span multiple lines (e.g. VSC EXT), then Software must ensure that the transcoder can complete transmitting all packets before the end of the Vblank

p.#text: This bit controls whether Forward Error Correction (FEC) is enabled on the port or not.
Programming Notes:

li.#text: Software shall not set this bit when operating in 128b/132b mode (the hardware will automatically enable FEC)
For 8b/10b mode:
FEC can be enabled at any time during mode-set, but Software must ensure the minimum amount of idle patterns have been sent before doing so (5 idle patterns in SST; 4 idle patterns in MST)

FEC can be disabled at any time outside of a mode-set for error recovery (i.e. the Sink did not detect the FEC_DECODE_EN message). When disabling, the transcoder will transmit the FEC_DECODE_DIS sequence at the next FEC_PM boundary (the FEC_DECODE_DIS will replace the FEC parity codes of the last FEC block)

After FEC is disabled, Software can re-enable at any time. Hardware will ensure it sends the FEC_DECODE_DIS sequence and satisfies all FEC disable protocols before sending a FEC_DECODE_EN to re-enable.

The data M and data N must account for the FEC overhead when FEC is enabled. Hardware will not adjust the data M/N values if FEC is disabled, nor does Software need to adjust this during error recovery (i.e. FEC is being disabled and then re-enabled).
Any function using ALPM (i.e., PSR, PSR2, PR, LOBF) cannot be active if disabling FEC.  Disable the function that uses ALPM before disabling FEC.

The hblank_early is generated on data timing (not the timing generator), so different factors such as the VDSC output bpp can shift the position of hblank_early relative to hblank. This 2-bit register field per transcoder within non-audio register space for early pixel count scaling provides guard bandwith to help insure that the actual position is at least greater than or equal to the value requested in AUD_CONFIG_BE.

The DP transcoder delivers an Early H.Blank to the Audio client so that it can pre-fill its pipeline and have Audio packets available before the transcoder reaches the H.Blank region. The AUD_CONFIG_BE[ HBlank_start count for Pipe * ] field defines how early the Transcoder needs to deliver the Early H.Blank where the units of measurement are dependent on the type of timing generator being used (i.e., Pixels when using the Pixel Based TG or Symbols when using the Symbol Based TG).

There are different factors (such as the VDSC output bpp) that can shift the position of the Early H.Blank relative to the actual H.Blank (specifically when using the Pixel Based TG). This field is used to multiply the H.Blank Start information from the Audio BE to create a guardband to help ensure the Early H.Blank is delivered before the transcoder reaches the H.Blank region.

This field specifies the ending frame for accumulate mode. The CRC engine will stop signature generation when the frame count is > end frame value. Setting this field to 0001b will cause the CRC engine to stop accumulating after the second frame pulse.

Software will set this bit when first entering the LTS:P state (i.e. Link Training has Passed).
Software will clear this bit when / if moves to the LTS:L state (i.e. going to the Legacy TMDS mode)

Note that disabling this bit after a successful link training will not cause the HDMI interface to start transmitting link training patterns (LTP) again. This is just a mechanism within hardware to gate FRL Character transmission until Software has completed a training sequence. To re-start link training, Software will need to disable the FRL Function.
This bit will disable throttling that the FRL link layer applies to RC compressible blank tri-bytes.
Throttling of the blank tri-bytes helps to mitigate line time contraction due to the depth of the Video Blank Pipeline.
When packets are being dispatched B2B (e.g. borrowing scenarios), the DFM will adjust down the number of resources available to the packet scheduling logic to account for pipeline delays.

However, if the number of available DFM resources is greater than the Maximum FRL Packet Payload Allowed + the maximum adjustment amount (maintained by HW), then the DFM will disable (or mask) the resource adjustment so that maximum sized packets can still be scheduled/dispatched.

When set, this bit will disable the adjustment masking logic which means that the FRL link layer will conservatively schedule packets less than the Maximum FRL Packet Payload Allowed when scheduling is in the presence of packets already being dispatched.

p.#text: This field controls how the FRL link layer schedules Active FRL Packets.

When Disabled, the FRL link layer will schedule Active FRL Packets without performing any resource checks against the Active Character data buffer (the pixel bandwidth from the core display should be able to maintain the bandwidth needed in the FRL Character domain)

When Enabled, the FRL link layer will only schedule Active FRL Packets when the Active Character data buffer has the specified number of FRL Characters present. The number of FRL Characters needed is specified through the Active Character Buffering Threshold field.
Notes for when resource-based scheduling is enabled:
Given the gaps that will be present between Active Video Packets, resource-based scheduling should not be enabled when a given VIC / Audio configuration requires time borrowing.
See the Transcoder HDMI 2.1 Support page for details on when resource-based scheduling will be required

li.#text: If Software does not program the Active Character Buffering Threshold field (i.e. it's left at its default value of zero), then the FRL link layer will default to scheduling a minimum of 32 Active Characters.

The FRL link layer will not schedule Active Video Packets larger than the threshold programming in the Active Character Buffering Threshold field (e.g. if the threshold is programmed for 32 Characters, then Active Video Packets will not carry payloads greater than 32 Characters)
The FRL link layer may schedule Active Video Packets that are smaller than the threshold programming in the threshold field depending on Data Flow Metering or when it has reached the end of the line.

The FRL link layer will not schedule / transmit Active Video Packets back to back (i.e. there will be Gap Characters between packets). At a minimum there will be 8 Gap Characters between packets (2 FRL Character clocks worth), but Data Flow Metering may insert more
This field can only be changed when the HDMI Transcoder is Disabled

p.#text: This field (when programmed to a non-zero value) enables resource checking logic for Active Video Character buffering within the FRL link layer. When left at its default value (zero), the FRL link layer will simply look for the Character data buffer to go non-empty.

When Resource Based Scheduling is Enabled, then this field will dictate how many Active FRL Characters need to be present within the data buffer before any Active FRL Packet is presented to the Packet Scheduling logic while dispatching an active line.

When Resource Based Scheduling is Disabled, then this field will dictate how many Active FRL Characters need to be present within the buffer before scheduling for a given active line is started. Once scheduling is started, no more resource checking will be done until the start of the next line.

li.#text: This field can only be changed when the HDMI Transcoder is Disabled

p.#text: This bit enables the Send Push bit to generate the Frame Change event when PSR, PSR2, or Panel Replay (PR) are active.
When not enabled, the PSR/PR logic will continue to use the legacy mechanism for detecting Frame Changes (looking at register write events within the Pixel Pipeline).
When enabled, the PSR/PR logic will ignore the register write events from the Pixel Pipeline and will wait for the Send Push to initiate an update to the Sink.
Notes:

li.#text: When Panel Replay with Link On is Active with VRR Enabled, the Send Push bit will initiate a selective update regardless of the programming of this bit (legacy behavior)

When the transcoder is operating in a fixed refresh rate when the PSR/PR functions are enabled (i.e. Vmin=Vmax=Flipline) the Send Push is technically not needed for this mode of operation. However, using the bit has no effect on the transcoder timings.

The legacy mechanism is non-atomic (i.e. Frame Change events are coming in for every register write that SW performs) and does not comprehend double buffer stalling (i.e. the transcoder will send out an update to the Sink on the next frame even if double buffer stalling is still being applied). Using the Send Push bit makes the Frame Change event to the transcoder atomic and ensures the update is sent to the Sink only after SW is finished with its updates.

This register sets the position for hardware to send the adaptive sync secondary data packet (SDP). That SDP defines the position of Vsync for DP to HDMI adaptive sync (VRR) supporting protocol converters. The HDMI requirement is for Vsync to be at a fixed position from the end of the Vblank (back porch). The TRANS_VSYNC register is not used for adaptive sync SDP because it provides Vsync position relative to the start of vertical active, which changes as adaptive sync shrinks or grows the initial portion of Vblank (front porch for HDMI).

This register sets the position for hardware to send the Vsync at a fixed position relative to the end of the Vblank (back porch) when VRR is enabled. The TRANS_VSYNC register is not used in VRR since it provides the Vsync position relative to the start of vertical active which changes as adaptive sync shrinks or grows the initial portion of Vblank (front porch).
This register sets the position for hardware to send the Vsync at a fixed position relative to the end of the Vblank (back porch)

This value specifies the vertical sync alignment for the start of the interlaced second field, expressed in terms of the absolute pixel number relative to the horizontal active display start.This value will only be used if the transcoder is programmed to an interlaced mode.Typically, the interlaced second field vertical sync should start one pixel after the point halfway between successive horizontal syncs, so the value of this register should be programmed = horizontal sync start - floor[horizontal total / 2]Calculate using the actual horizontal sync start and horizontal total values and not the minus one values programmed into the registers.This vertical sync shift only occurs during the interlaced second field. Description.#text: This field specifies Vertical Total size. Description.#text: Read by software/DSB to know if it can start sending new chain. Chained metadata straddling 2 buffers need to know this status.

p.#text: This field allows metadata to be replayed from the buffer without having to write the metadata buffer each time/frame.
This bit may only be changed when metadata buffer is invalidated.
This bit represents an error condition that not all SDPs were read when video active region is reached.
HW will stop transmitting metadata once active region is reached.
This bit is set by HW and cleared by SW by writing '1'.
To avoid false indication of an error, SW can choose either of the following methods:

li.#text: Avoid programming VSC_EXT registers and setting the buffer ready bit in VSC_EXT_SDP_CTL before vblank rises.

Program VSC_EXT registers and set the buffer ready bit in VSC_EXT_SDP_CTL anytime, but clear the SDP Active Error at the start of vblank, so that it can be rechecked at the end of vblank to indicate real issues.

@attributes.Name: All SDPs not transmitted in VBLANK

p.#text: When this bit is set to 1, it is software responsibility to set Middle Of Chaining bit [23] and Packet sequence bits [28:24] in the header packet that it programs in metadata register.
HW does not support changing this field during transmission.

@attributes.Name: Header values from SW/DSB written buffer

p.#text: In HW, this field is expressed in terms of pixels and not clocks.
It provides a guardband to stop the VSC_EXT_SDP transmission from going into Hblank region (for Audio).
For eg: If this field is programed to 20 pixels, then when horizontal counter reaches (HActive -20), VSC_EXT_SDP transmission stops.
If a packet is in the middle of transmission, then it completes before stopping. Transmission resumes on the next HActive.
In MST/DP2 this transmission can happen only when an MTP slot is available.
For all SST/MST/DP2 use cases, recommendation is to use 10% of HActive.
This field specifies the total number of packets (each packet has 32 bytes) in the chain.
= Number of bytes/32

span.#text: The VSC_EXT_VESA SDP allows a DP Source device to send video stream-related metadata aligned with the stream. A single VSC_EXT SDP is composed of four header bytes and 32 payload bytes. The VSC_EXT_VESA SDP maybe chained. Chaining framework enables a flexible metadata transportation framework to allow the transport of variable bytes of payload using a single VSC_EXT_VESA.
For transmitting frame synchronous metadata beyond 1KB, software must alternate between Buffer0 and Buffer1.
Metadata must be programmed in multiple of 32 bytes (8 dwords).

p.#text: This field allows Software to reset the read pointer of the metadata buffer.  Hardware will clear the bit after it has reset the read pointer.
This will be used by the DMC FW to reset the read pointer after doing a context save.
This field is set by hardware when buffer is empty and reset when buffer has metadata to be sent over the link.
This field is read by software (or DSB) to know when it can start writing to the buffer (buffer reuse cases included).

Description.#text: SW needs to check "buffer clear status" status bit in this register for re-transmission use cases.

p.#text: This field is set by software (or DSB) to indicate that the buffer is ready for hardware use.
Hardware clears this field after the buffer processing is complete.
SW can also clear this bit. Both SW clear and SW set will have higher priority over HW clear.

Description.#text: To ensure transmission of the packet(s) before the next frame, Software should ensure it programs the "Buffer Ready" bit before the transmission line of the VSC_EXT SDP.  See "Programming and Double Buffering of Data Island Packets"

p.#text: This field is set and reset by hardware.
Buffer is clear, and software can write the new HDR metadata
Buffers contents are valid and software cannot update the buffer.

Description.#text: This field controls the index auto increment.

p.#text: This field indicates the data location to be accessed through the data register. This value can be automatically incremented by a write to the data register if the index auto increment bit (14) is set. When automatically incrementing, the current automatically calculated index value can be read here, and the index will roll over to 0 after reaching the end of the allowed range.
8-bit index supports up to 1KB.
Examples:
00h =Dword at location 0

p.#text: This register defines the double buffer point and transmission line for DP/eDP Vendor Specific SDP's
Programming Notes:

li.#text: This register specifies a fixed position from the end of the Vblank (i.e. it defines the number of lines before the V. Active of the next frame that Software wants the packet to be transmitted on)
The double buffering for these packets is handled within the transcoders and not within the register block itself
The double buffering is done in the transcoder clock domain (e.g. the symbol clock domain). This means that the packet data will be clock crossed before it is double buffered
Restrictions on the position of the transmission line:
It must be within the SCL + Guardband region (i.e. VS_SDP_TL < (SCL + Guardband))
It must be within the non-delayed V. Blank region (i.e. (V. Active + 1) < (Vmin - VS_SDP_TL))
For DP/eDP, if there is a set context latency (SCL) window, then it cannot be the first line of SCL
For DP/eDP, if there is no SCL window, then it cannot be the first line of the Delayed V. Blank

To keep the clock crossing of the packet registers atomic, Software should program the packet data first and the packet header last. The clock crossing of all register data will be triggered off of the header write
Software should ensure that the packet header write is done before the line specified within this register.

This field selects the stream capture mode where WD captures data being sent to another port instead of acting as a port.

These bits select between different frame slicing options. Interlace means the capture will skip lines and only complete after multiple input frames. For example: 2:1 interlace captures lines 1, 3, 5, etc. on the first input frame, then 2, 4, 6, etc. on the second input frame, and full frame capture is complete after the second input frame completes.
This field enables stalling back to the pipe when the address is inserted in the writeback FIFO.
This bit will be set when the flushing read is not complete in stream capture mode.
This field gives the current slicing frame count (interlacing count). Count resets after reaching the selected interlace amount or disabling Stream Capture Mode, TRANS_CONF_WD, or TRANS_WD_FUNC_CTL.

This field is a sticky bit set when an input frame completes. If interlacing, then this may be only a partial frame. WD_FRAME_STATUS Frame Complete or WD Frame Complete interrupt indicates when a full frame is completely captured. Clear by writing a 1 to it.
SW should also check "Flushing Read Failure" register bit of this register.
This field is a sticky bit set when the writeback FIFO overflows. This is usually due to the input pixel stream running faster than WD can writeback to memory. Clear by writing a 1 to it.
